body:
Chief: MOCKUP REVIEW as asked. I inspected mockups/mockup1.png read-only (1536x1024 PNG, untracked, unattributed - I did not create it and I am not staging it). Architectural and scientific notes, and I am going to lead with what it gets right because the criticism is long.

=== WHAT IT GETS RIGHT, AND IT IS MORE THAN I EXPECTED ===

IT IS THE COORDINATED INSTRUMENT, NOT FIVE APPLICATIONS. Codex, Story Map, and Story-to-Recall Alignment share one workspace with one selection. Ep 2 / Scene 2.3 / "War party attacked" is selected in the tree, highlighted in the text, inspected on the right, and the alignment panel below is showing Scene 2.3. That is the split-workspace thesis actually drawn, and it answers the owner's requirement 2 - story and recall together, not "go to a different app".

SEMANTIC ZOOM IS DRAWN ON BOTH AXES. Bird's-eye tracks to codex lines to a single event inspector is the narrative axis; ZOOMED OUT recall coverage to ZOOMED IN sentence-level alignment is the same gesture applied to the recall. And "Drag to select region. Scroll to zoom. Click a track to focus" is continuous movement, not three radio buttons. That is requirement 1 as a product rather than a control.

THE ALIGNMENT PANEL IS THE BEST THING ON THE PAGE. Source sentences 98-103 against participant recall, with typed connectors - Exact, Partial/Gist, Misordered, Omitted, External. Five typed states rather than one fog is ADR 0002 D9 honoured. And "[skipped]" drawn as a first-class cell rather than a blank is exactly right.

=== NOW THE PROBLEMS, IN SEVERITY ORDER ===

1. "CONFIDENCE: 0.89" IS THE MOST DANGEROUS ELEMENT ON THE PAGE. Design-contract rule 3 is explicit: Credence.rawScore is NEVER a probability unless a calibrationModel is recorded. A bare "Confidence: 0.89" in an inspector reads as a calibrated probability to every researcher who sees it. If that number is an uncalibrated score wearing the word "confidence", it is the estimand defect promoted to the interface - and unlike the ones we fixed tonight, this one is read by a human who will quote it. EITHER IT CARRIES ITS CALIBRATION MODEL VISIBLY, OR IT IS NOT CALLED CONFIDENCE.

2. THERE IS NO VISUAL VOCABULARY FOR "WE COULD NOT ALIGN THIS", AND THAT IS ARTICLE II AT THE SURFACE. The alignment key has Exact, Partial/Gist, Misordered, Omitted, External. AlignState has a state we spent tonight defending: External(Unranked) - the aligner could not rank the unit at all. It is OUR failure, not the participant's behaviour. On this legend it can only land in "Omitted" or "External/Irrelevant", and BOTH ARE CLAIMS ABOUT THE PARTICIPANT. A researcher reading this panel would count our abstentions as their omissions. This is the exact defect we removed from internalRatio, from specificity, and from three route metrics, arriving through the front door.

3. "EXTERNAL / IRRELEVANT" COLLAPSES A TYPED VOCABULARY AND EDITORIALISES IT. AlignState's external destinations are Association, Intrusion, Commentary, SourceConsistentInference, Uninterpretable, Unranked. Six states, distinguished for scientific reasons. The legend shows one, and names it "Irrelevant" - which is a judgement no part of the model makes. D10 says recall visual vocabulary is GENERATED FROM AlignState. This legend is hand-authored and lossy, and the loss is exactly where the science lives.

4. FOUR AVERAGED TRACKS WITH NO SUPPORT: "Recall Coverage (avg)", "Recall Precision (average)", "Misordering (average)", "Omissions (average)". Article III - support travels with the estimate. An average over participants is mean-of-ratios unless it is a ratio-of-sums, and either way the reader needs the denominator. A coverage curve resting on two participants at one point and forty at another looks identical here. This is the compression defect at population scale, drawn as a smooth line.

5. THE SENSORY, SENTIMENT AND TENSION TRACKS NEED PROVENANCE. Auditory, Visual, Kinesthetic, Tension, Sentiment. If these are computed features, D11 binds - colour follows FeatureTarget and FeatureDerivation exactly - and each track owes its manifest. If any is inferred rather than derived, D4's no-inference law forbids it outright: no view creates a claim absent from the model ledger. A smooth continuous curve is the most persuasive object on a screen and the least self-evidencing.

6. "EVIDENCE (SENTENCES): 98-104" IS A RECONSTRUCTION IF IT EXPLAINS THE EVENT. Article V, and m1 established the mechanism this morning: the words that drove a cost are computed and discarded in the same expression. Names.overlap returns a Boolean. If that field means "these sentences are where this event was asserted", it is fine and span-backed. If it means "this is the evidence that produced this identification", it is a plausible account rather than the actual reason, and must be labelled.

=== ONE THING I CANNOT TELL FROM AN IMAGE, AND IT MATTERS MOST ===
Whether the horizon applies. ADR 0002 D14a, which I landed an hour ago, exists because marks a renderer adds itself are covered by neither V-L1, V-L2, nor the evidence horizon. This mockup shows sentence-level and token-adjacent detail everywhere. If any of it is drawn by the renderer from SurfaceAtlas rather than compiled into NarrativeScene, then a horizon-hidden node can have visible surface children. That is not a styling question; it is the leak we already fixed once.

VERDICT: this is a good product drawing and a scientifically dangerous one in four specific places, all of which are fixable in the vocabulary rather than the layout. The layout is right. The legend and the number labels are where the errors are, and those are the cheapest things on the page to change - now, before anyone builds to it.
